nav.dashboard.desc: Sidebar link to the dashboard (Alt+1). It opens the start page with the assigned game, today's gaming budget and the quick actions.

nav.backlog.desc: Sidebar link to the backlog page (Alt+2). It opens the planner, the completion-time stats and the full game list.

nav.picks.desc: Sidebar link to the picks page (Alt+3). It opens check, done, pick and scan, plus your manual picks.

nav.gaming.desc: Sidebar link to the gaming page (Alt+4). It opens the daily gaming budget with its reset, block and unblock actions.

nav.library.desc: Sidebar link to the library page (Alt+5). It opens every game you own, with install, uninstall and hide.

nav.store.desc: Sidebar link to the store page (Alt+6). It opens the timed store unblock, buying DLC and game exceptions.

nav.jobs.desc: Sidebar link to the jobs page (Alt+7). It lists the running and past jobs with their logs.

nav.system.desc: Sidebar link to the system page (Alt+8). It opens the root daemon, the web server, state backups, reset and setup.

palette.open.desc: Top-bar button (Ctrl+K) that opens the command palette. There you search for any command or section and run or open it.

cmd.status.desc: Opens the current status: the assigned game, its achievement progress and the enforcer's state.

cmd.list.desc: Opens the game list from the last scan snapshot, with achievements and completion times.

cmd.stats.desc: Opens the backlog estimates: how long the remaining games take to finish at your pace.

cmd.installed.desc: Opens the list of games installed on this PC, with the assigned and protected ones marked.

cmd.gaming-status.desc: Opens today's gaming time: minutes used, budget left and whether gaming is blocked.

cmd.check.desc: Runs check: looks for a new achievement on the assigned game. One new achievement releases the game.

cmd.scan.desc: Runs scan: reads the achievements of every owned game and assigns a game when none is set.

cmd.done.desc: Runs done: confirms a new achievement on the assigned game and moves on to pick the next one.

cmd.pick.desc: Runs pick: offers other candidate games to play next. It keeps the current game unless told to replace it.

cmd.pick-manual.desc: Runs a manual pick: you choose a game by hand and the enforcer locks onto it for some days.

cmd.abandon-pick.desc: Runs abandon pick: undoes a manual pick, so the enforcer assigns a game again.

cmd.install.desc: Runs install: downloads an allowed game, trying the fast installer first.

cmd.uninstall.desc: Runs uninstall: removes every installed game that is neither assigned nor protected.

cmd.repair-ghosts.desc: Runs repair ghosts: deletes the fake installed manifests anonymous steamcmd left, keeping any with staged bytes.

cmd.hide.desc: Runs hide: hides every game except the assigned one in the Steam library.

cmd.unhide.desc: Runs unhide: shows every game in the Steam library again.

cmd.buy-dlc.desc: Runs buy DLC: unblocks the Steam store for 15 minutes so you can buy a game or DLC.

cmd.unblock.desc: Runs unblock: opens the Steam store for a number of minutes, at most 30.

cmd.add-exception.desc: Runs add exception: allows one game right away, after a typed phrase and a logged reason.

cmd.block-gaming.desc: Runs block gaming: blocks all gaming for a number of days. There is no undo in the app.

cmd.reset.desc: Runs reset: wipes all enforcer state after saving a timestamped backup.

cmd.setup.desc: Opens setup: the Steam API key and the SteamID the enforcer needs.

cmd.enforce.desc: Runs the enforcer: block, uninstall, kill and hide. The demo runs a 60-second gaming budget only.

cmd.gaming-reset.desc: Runs gaming reset: resets today's gaming counter as root, after a typed phrase and a five-minute countdown.

cmd.gaming-unblock.desc: Runs gaming unblock: force-releases the playtime bind mounts. It is the root recovery hatch.

cmd.serve.desc: Restarts this web UI server. It comes back on the current code by itself.

cmd.re-block.desc: The daemon's end-of-window store re-block. It shows up as a job only when its checks failed.

cmd.restore-backup.desc: Restores a saved state backup after you type its phrase.

job.state.queued.desc: Job state badge: the job waits to start.

job.state.running.desc: Job state badge: the job is running now.

job.state.waiting_input.desc: Job state badge: the job is paused on a question and needs your answer.

job.state.succeeded.desc: Job state badge: the job finished without errors.

job.state.failed.desc: Job state badge: the job stopped on an error. Its log says why.

job.state.cancelled.desc: Job state badge: the job was stopped before it finished.

notice.info.desc: Mark on an information notice: a neutral fact or a hint.

notice.success.desc: Mark on a success notice: the action worked.

notice.warning.desc: Mark on a warning notice: something needs your attention, but nothing failed.

notice.danger.desc: Mark on an error notice: something failed or was refused. The server's message follows it.

state.yes.desc: Marks a yes in a row: the thing is on, present, current or matching.

state.no.desc: Marks a no in a row: the thing is missing, off or does not match.

state.off.desc: Marks an empty value in a row: off, none or not set.

state.warn.desc: Marks a row or label that needs attention: stale, unavailable or not ready. Nothing has failed yet.

state.wait.desc: Shows that a button or row is busy: saving, sending, restarting or counting down.

state.empty.desc: Empty state: there is nothing to show yet, such as no data or no games.

state.unknown.desc: Unknown value: the data is missing or its kind is not recognised. It also shows a play style that is not known yet.

state.locked.desc: Locked: the command or action cannot run right now. The reason is read aloud.

state.unlocked.desc: Unlocked: the action is open and free to use.

action.cancel.desc: Button that cancels or closes the open form, dialog or countdown without doing anything.

action.confirm.desc: Button that confirms: it saves the form or sends the answer.

action.open.desc: Link on a card that opens the page behind it, such as the details or the full list.

copy.command.desc: Button that copies a shell command to the clipboard. It is the way out when the UI cannot act itself.

copy.done.desc: Replaces the copy button for two seconds after the copy worked.

dash.ago.desc: Shown before a time span that says how long ago something happened, such as a recent job or the live verdict.

dash.finished.desc: Marks the number of games you finished with every achievement. It labels the dashboard row and the base of your pace estimate.

dash.store.desc: Row label on the dashboard: whether the Steam store is blocked right now.

dash.store-blocked.desc: Value of the store row on the dashboard: the Steam store is blocked.

dash.store-open.desc: Value of the store row on the dashboard: the Steam store is unblocked for now. It blocks itself again later.

dash.games.desc: Row label on the dashboard: how many games are installed on this PC.

dash.total-block.desc: Row label on the dashboard: the total gaming block. While it is active the row counts down the time left.

picks.manual.desc: Marks your manual picks, the games you locked in by hand. It heads the picks card and labels the dashboard row.

assigned.game.desc: Marks the game assigned to you. It heads the assignment card, tags the game in the library and sits beside the live verdict.

dash.block-left.desc: Time left on the total gaming block, shown as a countdown.

dash.budget.desc: Heading of the budget card on the dashboard. It shows how much gaming time is left today.

dash.blocked-today.desc: Shown on the budget card when gaming is blocked for the rest of the day.

dash.not-billing.desc: Shown while no game is running, so no gaming time is used. It marks the budget line and the live verdict.

dash.billing.desc: Shown while a game is running and its time counts against today's budget. It marks the budget line and the live verdict.

dash.fast-failed.desc: A fast install failed. The daemon's own message follows it.

dash.steam-took-over.desc: Note under a failed fast install: Steam's own download took over.

dash.fast-install.desc: A fast install is running. It heads the fast install card and marks each running download.

dash.elapsed.desc: Time a fast install has been running so far.

dash.recent-jobs.desc: Heading of the recent jobs card on the dashboard. It lists the last five jobs with their state.

dash.outlook.desc: Heading of the backlog outlook card on the dashboard: the planner summary at the default filters.

picks.age.desc: Marks how many days ago a manual pick was made. The app id follows it.

picks.kept.desc: Marks a pick that was released but kept: the game stays installed and playable.

store.blocked.desc: Notice on the store page: the Steam store is blocked. Unblocking takes a typed phrase and lasts at most 30 minutes.

store.open.desc: Notice on the store page: the Steam store is open right now. It blocks itself again after the timer runs out.

setup.help.desc: Link next to a setup field that opens the page where you get the value.

setup.key-stored.desc: Shown when the Steam API key is already stored, in the setup field and the system row. The key stays hidden, and typing a new key replaces it.

setup.api-key.desc: Marks the Steam Web API key: the field on the setup page where you paste it, and the system row that shows if one is stored.

setup.steam-id.desc: Marks the SteamID: the field on the setup page for your 17-digit profile number, and the system row that shows it.

libpage.all.desc: Switch on the library page that shows every game you own as a cover grid.

libpage.game.desc: Marks a game: the game column of the installed table and the number of installed games.

libpage.app-id.desc: Header of the app id column in the installed table: the Steam number of each game.

libpage.size.desc: Size on disk: the size column header and the total of all installed games.

libpage.role.desc: Header of the role column in the installed table: whether a game is assigned, protected or removable.

libpage.protected.desc: Tags an installed game that is protected, so uninstall never removes it.

libpage.candidate.desc: Marks an installed game that is neither assigned nor protected, so uninstall would remove it.

jobs.command.desc: Header of the command column in the job history.

jobs.state.desc: Header of the state column in the job history: queued, running, finished or failed.

jobs.started.desc: When a job started: the started column of the job history and the created time on a job page.

jobs.took.desc: Header of the duration column in the job history: how long each job ran.

jobs.not-found.desc: Marks a job page whose id does not exist. The history keeps only the last 50 jobs.

jobs.all.desc: Link to the job history list, shown on a job page and on a missing job.

jobs.job.desc: Heading of a job page while the job loads.

jobs.waiting.desc: Phase mark on a job page when the job waits for your answer.

jobs.cancel.desc: Button on a running job that asks it to stop. It appears only for jobs that can be cancelled.

jobs.log.desc: Marks the job log: it shows the number of log lines and opens the log.

prompt.question.desc: Marks a question a job asks you. The job waits until you answer.

prompt.own-game.desc: Choice in a job question that lets you pick any game from your library instead of the offered ones.

prompt.yes.desc: Button that answers yes to a job question.

prompt.no.desc: Button that answers no to a job question.

prompt.answer.desc: Button that sends your answer to a job question. The Enter key does the same.

prompt.back.desc: Button that returns from the game picker to the previous question of the job.

prompt.games.desc: Shows how many games a job offers to pick from in a game question.

prompt.pick.desc: Button that sends the game you selected as the answer. It shows the game name once you select one.

jobchip.needs-input.desc: Shown on a job chip in the top bar when the job waits for your answer.

dash.installed.desc: Marks a game that is installed on this PC. It labels the dashboard row, the library filter and table, and the badge on a game.

gaming.series.other.desc: Legend and list entry that groups the many small games of the chart into one segment.

gaming.series.unattributed.desc: Legend entry for gaming time that no single game could be charged for.

gaming.launcher.desc: Marks a game launcher such as a store client. It also labels the rule that counts launcher time against the budget.

gaming.cutoff.masked.desc: Badge on a blocked day: the cutoff is engaged and the launchers are masked, so no game can start.

gaming.cutoff.unmasked.desc: Badge on a blocked day: the cutoff is engaged but no launcher is masked right now. That happens after a total block released the mounts.

gaming.warn.none.desc: Shows that no further warning fires today. The enforcer has already sent the last one.

gaming.warning.desc: The time of the next warning on today's card and the warning times in the rules card. The enforcer warns you when the remaining budget reaches them.

gaming.day.desc: The date of the gaming day that today's budget belongs to.

gaming.day_start.desc: The local time when the gaming day rolls over and the budget refills.

gaming.by_game.desc: Heading of the list that splits today's billed time by game.

gaming.right_now.desc: Heading of the live card with the daemon's latest verdict on what the budget is charging.

gaming.qualifying.desc: The number of running processes that count as gaming and bill the budget.

gaming.billing_to.desc: Names the game or launcher that the budget is charging right now.

gaming.billed_last.desc: Names the game or launcher that was charged last, once nothing qualifies any more.

gaming.history.desc: Heading of the chart with the billed gaming time of each of the last 14 days.

gaming.rules.desc: Heading of the card that lists the budget rules the enforcer applies right now.

gaming.budget.desc: Row label for how much gaming time one day allows.

gaming.enforcement.desc: Row label that shows whether the enforcer cuts off gaming when the budget runs out.

gaming.mode.desc: Row label for the budget mode, the real one or the demo.

gaming.demo.desc: Marks the short demo budget with its separate state. As a link it switches the page to that demo.

gaming.masked.desc: Row label that lists the launchers masked right now, so that they cannot start.

gaming.production.desc: Link shown on the demo page that switches back to the real daily budget.

daemon.heading.desc: The root daemon that enforces the rules. It heads the daemon card and is the daemon badge in the top bar.

daemon.demo_run.desc: Button that opens the runner for a 60-second demo of the enforcer with a short budget.

daemon.journal.desc: Heading of the live tail of the daemon's log.

daemon.state.desc: Row label for the daemon's current state.

daemon.running.desc: Daemon state: the daemon is up and answers.

daemon.restarting.desc: Daemon state: the daemon is restarting and answers again in a moment.

daemon.unreachable.desc: Daemon state: the daemon does not answer, so the privileged actions are unavailable.

daemon.pid.desc: Row label for the process number of the running daemon.

daemon.up_since.desc: Row label for how long the daemon has been running.

daemon.restart.desc: Button that restarts the root daemon. A rate limit allows it only now and then.

server.heading.desc: The web server that serves this UI. It heads the server card and is the server badge in the top bar.

server.version.desc: Row label for the version of the running web server.

server.started.desc: Row label for the time the web server process started.

server.code.desc: Row label that compares the code on disk with the running server. A warning means the server runs old code.

server.restart.desc: Button that restarts the web server, on the server card and in the stale-server banner. The page reloads when the server is back.

backup.item.desc: Heading of the card with the saved state backups, and the mark in front of one backup in the restore dialog.

backup.reason.reset.desc: Reason mark: the backup was taken right before a reset wiped the state.

backup.reason.nightly.desc: Reason mark: the backup was taken by the nightly timer.

backup.reason.other.desc: Reason mark for a backup whose reason the UI does not know.

backup.restore.desc: Button that restores the state from a backup. It first asks for a typed phrase.

syssetup.configured.desc: Row label that shows whether setup is complete.

syssetup.edit.desc: Link that opens the setup page, where the key and the SteamID can be changed.

gaming.today.desc: Heading of the card with today's budget numbers on the gaming page.

basis.rush.desc: Rush estimate: how long the games take at a fast completionist pace. It is a choice in the filter panel, a card in the summary and a column in the table.

basis.leisure.desc: Leisure estimate: how long the games take at a slow, comfortable pace. It is a choice in the filter panel, a card in the summary and a column in the table.

basis.worst.desc: Worst-case estimate: the longest time anyone has recorded for each game. It is a choice in the filter panel, a card in the summary and a column in the table.

basis.pace.desc: Your own pace: the estimate built from how fast you finished games before. It marks the pace choice, the pace card and your play-style block.

style.fast.desc: Play style: you finish games faster than the fast times on HowLongToBeat.

style.between.desc: Play style: your pace sits between the rush and leisure times on HowLongToBeat.

style.slow.desc: Play style: you finish games slower than the slow leisure times on HowLongToBeat.

tier.native.desc: ProtonDB tier native: the game runs on Linux without Proton. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.platinum.desc: ProtonDB tier platinum: the game runs perfectly under Proton out of the box. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.gold.desc: ProtonDB tier gold: the game runs perfectly after small tweaks. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.silver.desc: ProtonDB tier silver: the game is playable with minor issues. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.bronze.desc: ProtonDB tier bronze: the game runs but with frequent problems. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.borked.desc: ProtonDB tier borked: the game does not run at all. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

tier.pending.desc: ProtonDB tier pending: there are not enough reports to rate the game yet. It shows in the tier column and the tier filters.

keep.kept.desc: Value of the keep filter: the game stays in the plan. Choosing it shows only the kept games.

keep.excluded.desc: Value of the keep filter: you took the game out of the plan. Choosing it shows only the dropped games.

backlog.any.desc: Any value: in a filter it sets no limit and shows every game.

backlog.cli.desc: Stands for the command-line tool's own rule. It marks the playable rule, the default game count and what reset restores.

filter.reset.desc: Button in the filter panel that sets every filter back to the CLI defaults.

filter.min-tier.desc: Choice of the ProtonDB filter: keep games at or above a minimum tier that you pick.

filter.started.desc: Choice of the playtime filter: only games you have already started.

filter.untouched.desc: Choice of the playtime filter: only games with no playtime at all.

filter.daily.desc: Slider for how many hours you play each day. The time estimates divide by it.

planner.completions.desc: How many completion times HowLongToBeat holds for a game. It is a table column and the minimum slider in the filter panel.

filter.min-polled.desc: Slider for the fewest polled completionist times a game needs to count.

filter.min-confidence.desc: Slider for the minimum confidence sum, the total weight of the time reports behind an estimate.

filter.max-time.desc: Slider for the longest game you accept. Longer games are hidden.

filter.no-cap.desc: Shown in place of the hours when the time cap is off.

filter.fallback.desc: Slider for the hours guessed for games that have no time data.

filter.basis.desc: Heading of the estimate-basis choice: rush, leisure, worst case or your pace.

filter.advanced.desc: Heading of the folded advanced confidence settings. Opening it shows two more sliders.

planner.proton.desc: ProtonDB: how well a game runs on Linux. It heads the compatibility filter and the table column.

filter.proton-missing.spoken: Keep games with no ProtonDB data
filter.proton-missing.desc: Checkbox in the compatibility filter: keep games that have no ProtonDB data in the list.

planner.playtime.desc: Your playtime in a game. It heads the playtime filter and the table column.

planner.no-data.desc: Badge on a game that has no HowLongToBeat data. The checkbox with the same mark includes such games, using the fallback hours.

filter.target-date.desc: Target finish date: the filter's date field and the by-date marker in the banner. It turns hours into the daily pace you need.

filter.clear-date.desc: Button that clears the target finish date.

backlog.sort-asc.desc: Marks the table column that is sorted from low to high.

backlog.sort-desc.desc: Marks the table column that is sorted from high to low.

planner.game.desc: Table column with the game names. Clicking its header sorts by name.

planner.completion.desc: Table column with each game's achievement completion in percent.

planner.keep.desc: Table column with the checkbox that keeps a game in the plan or drops it.

summary.to-finish.desc: Banner on the backlog page: how many games are left to finish by your target date.

summary.games-per-day.desc: Unit on the pace card and banner: games finished per day. It follows the number.

backlog.in-scope.desc: Count of games that pass the filters. It sits beside the big number in the summary and in the stats card.

summary.need.desc: Arrow in the target banner between the chosen model and the daily time you need.

summary.no-start.desc: Shown on the pace card when no start date is set, so there is no finish date.

summary.style.desc: Label of the play-style row: how your pace compares with the HowLongToBeat times.

summary.interpolation.desc: Label of the blend value t. It is 0 at rush speed and 1 at leisure speed.

summary.estimated-total.desc: Label of your estimated total time to finish all games at your pace.

summary.match.desc: Shown when the number of games in scope equals the CLI default.

planner.playing.desc: On the planner header: the game you are playing right now.

planner.since.desc: On the planner header: the date the enforcer started counting.

planner.candidates.desc: On the planner header: how many games the planner can pick from.

stats.card.desc: Heading of the estimates card on the backlog page. It shows the totals for the default filters.

backlog.filters.desc: Heading of the filter panel on the backlog page. Its sliders and switches narrow the game list.

cmdflag.root.desc: Flag on a command: it runs as root through the daemon. It shows on the command card and in the run dialog.

cmdflag.countdown.desc: Flag on a command: it asks for a countdown before it can be committed. In the run dialog it carries the minutes.

cmdflag.mutating.desc: Flag in the run dialog: this command changes state on your PC or in the enforcer.

cmdflag.readonly.desc: Flag in the run dialog: this command only reads and changes nothing.

cmdflag.cancellable.desc: Flag in the run dialog: a running job of this command can be stopped.

cmdpal.search.desc: Search field of the command palette. Typing narrows the list of commands and pages.

cmdpal.run-phrase.desc: Hint on a palette entry: choosing it opens the run dialog, where you must type a phrase first.

cmdpal.open.desc: Hint on a palette entry for a command that only views data: choosing it opens the page that shows it.

cmdpal.go.desc: Hint on a palette entry for a page: choosing it navigates there.

runner.run.desc: Button that runs the command in the run dialog. The palette shows it as the hint on entries that run one.

runner.arm.desc: Submit button for a command with a countdown: it arms the countdown instead of running at once.

runner.fill.desc: Hint in the run dialog: the exact phrase appears once the fields above are filled in.

runner.terminal.desc: Shown when the root daemon is unreachable. The command beside it runs the same job from a terminal.

params.app_id.desc: Field in the run dialog: the game to act on, by app id or by picking its name.

params.backup_id.desc: Field in the run dialog: which saved state backup to use.

params.days.desc: Field in the run dialog: how many days the action lasts.

params.minutes.desc: Field in the run dialog: how many minutes the action lasts.

params.reason.desc: Field in the run dialog: why you do this. The reason is logged.

params.replace.desc: Switch in the run dialog: replace the current game instead of keeping it.

params.demo.desc: Switch in the run dialog: run the short demo budget instead of the real one.

params.other.desc: Marks any run-dialog field that has no icon of its own.

phrase.field.desc: Label of the typed-phrase field. You retype the shown sentence, and pasting is blocked.

pending.leave.desc: Warning during a countdown: closing the dialog or leaving the page cancels it.

pending.rearm.desc: Button shown when the countdown lapsed: it starts the command over.

pending.beat.desc: Seconds since the last heartbeat that keeps the countdown alive. It turns into a broken heart when beats fail.

pending.beat-lost.desc: Replaces the heartbeat while beats fail. The countdown lapses if they do not recover.

lib.sort.desc: Label of the sort menu in the game browser. The menu orders the grid by name, last played, completion or length.

lib.name.desc: Sort option: games in alphabetical order by name.

lib.recent.desc: Sort option: the games you played most recently come first.

lib.completion.desc: Share of achievements unlocked. It is a sort option and the first part of each game's meta line.

lib.hltb.desc: Hours that How Long To Beat lists for the game. It is a sort option, shortest first, and part of the meta line.

lib.played.desc: Hours you have played the game, shown in its meta line.

lib.hide-completed.desc: Filter in the game browser: hide the games you have finished.

lib.pickable.desc: Filter in the game browser: show only the games the enforcer lets you pick.

lib.count.desc: Count in the game browser: the games shown before the slash, the games in total after it.

lib.relevance.desc: Appears beside the count while a search ranks the games by relevance. The sort menu is off then.

lib.search.desc: Search field of the game browser. Typing filters the grid and lists suggestions.

lib.why.complete.desc: Reason a game cannot be picked: all its achievements are done.

lib.why.noach.desc: Reason a game cannot be picked: it has no achievements to earn.

lib.why.skipped.desc: Reason a game cannot be picked: it was skipped until the date shown beside it.

lib.why.blocked.desc: Reason a game cannot be picked, for any other cause. The server's sentence is spoken.

health.ok.desc: State mark on a health badge: all is well.

health.warn.desc: State mark on a health badge: the server runs stale code or the daemon is restarting.

health.bad.desc: State mark on a health badge: the server is down or the daemon is unreachable.

health.unknown.desc: State mark on a health badge before the daemon state is known.

health.stale.desc: Banner mark: the running server is older than the code on disk. The restart button beside it fixes that.

dialog.close.desc: Close button in the corner of every dialog.

words.page.desc: Command palette entry that opens this icon-words picker. You are here now.

params.target.desc: Install dialog field: an AppID, a Steam URL or a name. Only games allowed today install; an ambiguous name asks you to pick.

params.dry_run.desc: Switch in the install dialog: show what the installer would do and change nothing.

params.valve_proton.desc: Switch in the install dialog: keep the game on Valve's default Proton instead of the mapped one.

result.dry-run.desc: Mark on an install result: it was a dry run, nothing was installed or changed.

result.game-running.desc: Mark on an install result: a game was running, so the fast installer (which closes Steam) was skipped and Steam's own download started.
